title: Kaspa vProgs: Smart Contracts Without an L2
description:
Kaspa ($KAS) is building vProgs: verifiable programs, real apps on a proof of work base layer, not on an L2. Kaspa is never going to run your app. Kaspa is going to verify it. That one flip is how you get apps with proof of work security and no L2 in the middle.

Back in 2020 Vitalik put Ethereum all in on rollups, and every rollup comes with its own sequencer, its own bridge and its own slice of liquidity. Every one of those pieces is a place for something to break. Kaspa's founder, Yonatan Sompolinsky, calls that the obsolete path of L2s. So I break down how a vProg actually works: the four jobs Kaspa does, who runs the app, and how a zero-knowledge proof lets Kaspa check the math instead of redoing it.

Then I walk the ladder of where this all stands, from 10 blocks a second to Toccata live on mainnet to Silverscript 1.0, and what is still under construction.
